content: Macrocephaly refers to an increased head circumference, which is when the measured distance around the widest part of the skull is larger than expected for a child’s age and background. Symptoms of Macrocephaly: Increased intracranial pressure (elevated pressure within the skull) often accompanies an enlarged head circumference. Symptoms associated with this condition may include: Downward deviation of the eyes (commonly referred to as sunsetting eyes). Irritability. Vomiting. Causes of Macrocephaly: Benign familial macrocephaly (a hereditary tendency for larger head size). Canavan disease. Hurler syndrome. Hydrocephalus, which may be congenital, post-traumatic, or obstructive in nature. Intracranial bleeding. Morquio syndrome. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care: Macrocephaly is often identified during routine well-baby examinations by a healthcare provider. The healthcare provider will take a detailed medical history and perform a thorough physical examination. Questions during the medical history may include: Time pattern: When did you first notice that the baby’s head appeared larger than normal? Is the head size increasing more rapidly compared to the growth of the rest of the body? Location: Does the head appear uniformly larger, or is the growth more pronounced in a front-to-back or side-to-side pattern? Other symptoms: Are there any additional symptoms, particularly changes in brain or nervous system functions? Diagnostic Process: The head circumference is measured in centimeters or inches and compared to: Previous measurements of the child’s head circumference. Normal ranges for the child’s sex and age, based on standard growth rates for infants and children. A careful physical examination will be conducted, and other developmental milestones will be assessed. In some cases, a single measurement may confirm the need for further testing. However, repeated measurements over time are often necessary to confirm that the head circumference is increasing and that the condition is worsening. Diagnostic tests may vary depending on the suspected cause but often include: A head CT scan. An MRI of the head. Where to Find Medical Care for Macrocephaly: Consult a pediatrician or a specialist in pediatric neurology or genetics for further evaluation and management of macrocephaly.
